newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen shares end up on earnings hope.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen shares end up on earnings hope.

text.p: Shenzhen's A and B share indices closed up on Friday due in part to demand for counters promising solid earnings for last year, with investors shrugging off concerns about Beijing's plan to curb the flow of bank funds into the equity market, brokers said.
The B share index gained 1.51 points or 1.06 percent to close at 143.16 on turnover of HK$53.63 million, compared with Thursday's HK$31.70 million.
The A share index advanced 3.76 points or 1.10 percent to end at 346.62 on turnover of 4.28 billion yuan against 3.06 billion yuan in the previous session.

The Shenzhen-based Securities Times on Friday quoted China's vice premier Zhu Rongji as saying at a national bankers meeting in Beijing that people found to be using bank funds to trade stocks will face severe punishment.
But talk on the policy had been circulating in the market for several sessions and investors had digested it, brokers said.
"The policy will weaken demand for shares for the time being but will benefit the market over the long term," a broker with a major Chinese brokerage said.
Investors were seen carefully building positions in firms likely to post healthy results for 1996, brokers said.

On the B share market, China Marine Container, the biggest gainer, rose HK$0.28 or 3.22 percent to HK$8.98 on volume of 335,241 shares due to investor confidence in the company's 1996 profits, brokers said.
Building materials producer Fangda climbed HK$0.23 to HK$8.24 on trade of 745,782 shares, making it the day's third most active counter.
Changan Automobile rose HK$0.05 to HK$4.52 after 723,405 shares changed hands.
Guangdong Power put in the weakest performance and declined HK$0.06 to HK$6.89 on the session's heaviest trade of 1.51 million shares due to institutional selling, brokers said.
Hubei-based welding materials producer Monkey King was the strongest A share performer and jumped 0.84 yuan or 9.76 percent to 9.45 yuan on heavy volume of 14.31 million shares.
